newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar will have to wait for new peaks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar will have to wait for new peaks.

text.p: Technicians foresee fresh peaks for the dollar in the week ahead, but expect a good deal of range-trading before any new highs are set.

"In the bigger picture we haven't done anything to break the uptrend in dollar/mark or dollar/yen," said Thom Worden, vice president in the global technical analysis group at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
In dollar/mark, Worden said he is looking for a near-term climb above 1.7330 with an extension through to 1.7450. He said a failure to see such a rise would suggest downside potential.
"While we're below 1.7330 the risk is still slightly to the downside," Worden said, calling that level a trendline off the price action of the last few days.
On the downside, Worden saw initial support at Friday's low of roughly 1.72 and said a drop below there would spur a test of 1.7170 and perhaps stronger support at 1.7140.

At 1530 EDT/1930 GMT on Friday, the dollar was trading hands at 1.7285/95 marks and 126.58/63 yen. Chartists said the dollar's upside potential versus the yen was being capped by fears of central bank intervention.

"I still think there's a chance you'll see 129 in dollar/yen, but with the fear of intervention it's probably going to be a pretty slow grind," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America.
Johnson pegged good resistance between 127.20 and 127.40, with support at 126.20, 126.00 and 125.70.
While he predicted new highs for both dollar/mark and dollar/yen, he said signs were emerging that the dollar could be close to an intermediate-term top.
"In the bigger picture I think you get a blow off rally and go to new highs, that sucks everyone in, and then it drops out dramatically," he said.
